function.name: religion_history_get_councils
function.description: Retrieves a list of major councils in a specified religion. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

religion.description: Name of the religion for which to retrieve the councils.

count.description: Number of top councils to retrieve.

function.name: religion_history_get_reformations
function.description: Retrieves a list of major reformations in a specified religion. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

religion.description: Name of the religion for which to retrieve the reformations.

count.description: Number of top reformations to retrieve.

function.name: religion_history_get_schisms
function.description: Retrieves a list of major schisms in a specified religion. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

religion.description: Name of the religion for which to retrieve the schisms.

count.description: Number of top schisms to retrieve.

message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Date | Key Parties Involved | Main Causes |
|---|--------|------------------|----------------------|-------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 CE | Eastern Orthodox Church vs. Roman Catholic Church | Doctrinal differences (e.g., Filioque clause, papal primacy), cultural and political tensions between the Byzantine and Latin worlds. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | Various Protestant movements (Lutheran, Calvinist, Anglican, etc.) vs. Roman Catholic Church | Corruption in the Church, theological disputes (e.g., justification by faith), desire for vernacular liturgy, and the rise of national churches. |
| 3 | **East–West Schism of 1965 (also called the “Second Great Schism” in some contexts)** | 1965 CE | Eastern Orthodox Church vs. Roman Catholic Church (in the context of the 1965 *Intercommunion* discussions) | Continued theological and ecclesiological differences, especially regarding the nature of the Holy Spirit and the role of the Pope; the 1965 discussions highlighted unresolved issues that led to a renewed sense of separation. |

These schisms shaped the development of Christianity, leading to the formation of distinct traditions and influencing religious, cultural, and political landscapes across the world.
